points.description: Recognises that with buffer size 10, fewer than 10 packets are waiting in every state except the full state, so the answer is based on the probability of the system not being full (1 − blocking probability P_B, or summing probabilities of 0–9 packets), using utilization 0.9 in an M/M/1/N-type formula.
points.partial_credit: Half if the student only says to use blocking probability / state probabilities without linking it to the full state or without using utilization 0.9.

points.description: Multiplies the 60 s observation time by the probability of not being full (1 − P_B, with P_B about 0.05) to get about 57 seconds (56.95).
points.partial_credit: Half if the student multiplies 60 by a probability with the right idea but gets the number wrong, or gives about 57 s with little justification.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the idea that the system is below 10 unless full (blocking probability), and that the expected time is 60 × (1 − P_B), about 57 s. Give part marks for a right-track answer that is vague or has an arithmetic slip. Give no marks for answers with no queueing-probability reasoning and no time calculation. Different wording and informal steps are fine.
